questions.stem: Which of the following tables exist within the GRC: Profiles application scope? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The GRC: Profiles application scope (sn_grc) contains the foundational parent tables: sn_grc_document (Document), sn_grc_content (Content), sn_grc_item (Item), sn_grc_profile (Entity/Profile), sn_grc_profile_type (Entity Type), and sn_grc_indicator (Indicator). Policy (B) is in the Policy and Compliance scope, and Risk (C) is in the Risk Management scope. Document (A), Content (D), and Indicator (E) are all within the GRC: Profiles scope.

questions.stem: What are some characteristics of the ServiceNow Store? (Choose four.)

options.text: Some applications are certified by ServiceNow
All applications are certified by ServiceNow
Applications may be developed by ServiceNow Technology Partners
It houses both paid and free applications and integrations
Applications are built om the ServiceNow platform
Applications are certified by other developers

questions.explanation: The ServiceNow Store hosts apps built on the ServiceNow platform (E), developed by both ServiceNow and Technology Partners (C), with a mix of paid and free apps (D). Some apps are certified by ServiceNow (A), but not all — partner apps may not be certified by ServiceNow. 'All applications are certified' (B) is incorrect since partners can publish without full ServiceNow certification. 'Certified by other developers' (F) is not a Store characteristic.

questions.stem: Which role is not part of ServiceNow GRC?
questions.explanation: GRC Risk roles include sn_risk.user (Risk User), sn_risk.manager (Risk Manager), sn_risk.admin (Risk Admin), and sn_risk.reader (Risk Reader). There is no 'Risk Developer' role in ServiceNow GRC. Developer roles exist for the platform (e.g., app_developer) but not specifically for the risk module.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true of a Risk Response task?

options.text: Only one Risk Response task can be related to a Risk at a time
Only users with the risk_manager role or higher can be assigned to a Risk Response task
The risk admin role is required to assign the Risk Response task
The Risk Response task is automatically progressed through the states using a workflow

questions.explanation: Risk Response tasks in ServiceNow GRC are progressed through their states automatically using a workflow. Multiple response tasks can exist per risk (not limited to one, so A is wrong). Any user with the risk_user role or higher can be assigned (B is wrong). The risk_user role is sufficient to assign tasks (C is wrong — risk_admin is not specifically required).

questions.stem: What table, along with the Policy table, is linked to the Control Objective table by a many-to-many relationship?
questions.explanation: Control Objectives (sn_compliance_policy_statement) have many-to-many relationships with both the Policy table and the Citation table. The m2m table sn_compliance_m2m_statement_citation links Control Objectives to Citations. Authority Documents (C) and Risk Framework (D) extend the Document table but don't have a direct m2m with Control Objectives.

questions.stem: Why would you create Entity classes?

options.text: To show relationships between tables or objects you are tracking that doesn’t otherwise exist anywhere in ServiceNow
To be assigned to risk statements, which generate risks for every Entity listed in the Entity Class
To be assigned to Control Objectives, which generate Controls for every Entity listed in the Entity class
To show relationships between Entities and Policies and map them directory to Citations

questions.explanation: Entity Classes group entities to show relationships between tables or objects being tracked, enabling dependency modeling that doesn't otherwise exist in ServiceNow. They support the GRC Workbench dependency map for visualizing upstream/downstream relationships. Entity Classes are NOT assigned to risk statements (B) or control objectives (C) — Entity Types serve that purpose. Entity Classes don't map directly to Citations (D).

questions.stem: The Tablename.config:

options.text: Displays the configuration list view of the table in the browser tab
Displays the table in list view within the Content Frame
Displays the table in list view within a separate browser tab
Displays the configuration list view of the table in the Content Frame

questions.explanation: The .config syntax in the ServiceNow filter navigator displays the configuration list view of the specified table within the Content Frame (the main area of the platform UI). It does not open a separate browser tab (A, C). It shows the configuration/settings view, not a standard list view (B).

questions.stem: Which of the following extends from items?
questions.explanation: The Item table (sn_grc_item) is a parent table extended by Risk (sn_risk_risk) and Control (sn_compliance_control). Citation (A) extends Content (sn_grc_content). Issue (C) has its own table (sn_grc_issue). Policy (D) extends the Document table (sn_grc_document). Of the options given, Controls (B) extend from Items.

questions.stem: What happens when you assign an Entity Type to a Risk Statement?

options.text: An assessment will be automatically generated to test each Entity listed in the Entity Type
A risk assessment is created automatically for every Entity listed in the Entity Type
A risk is automatically generated for every Entity listed in the Entity Type
The Entity is now going to present a risk score and controls are going to be tied to it

questions.explanation: When an Entity Type is assigned to a Risk Statement, a risk is automatically generated for every entity listed in that Entity Type. This is the core of entity scoping — Entity Types map to Risk Statements to auto-create risk instances. It does not create assessments (A, B) or tie controls to entities (D) — those happen when Entity Types are scoped on Control Objectives.

questions.stem: There is a direct relationship between Entity Class and Entity Type when:

options.text: They have the same Entity Types

questions.explanation: There is no direct relationship between Entity Class and Entity Type in ServiceNow GRC. Entity Types group entities based on source tables (e.g., departments, locations) and are used for auto-generating risks and controls. Entity Classes group entities for reporting and advanced risk assessment purposes. They serve different functions and operate independently.

questions.stem: Which filter navigation syntax displays the table in list view within a separate browser tab?
questions.explanation: The .LIST syntax (all caps) in the ServiceNow filter navigator opens the table in list view within a separate browser tab. The lowercase .list displays the list view in the Content Frame. Tablename_LIST (A) is not valid syntax. Tablename.List (D) with mixed case is not the correct format.

questions.stem: Jim is an Audit Manager. In addition to Audit Manager, which roles should be assigned to ensure he can manage the audit process as well as other GRC functions related to audit? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: An Audit Manager (sn_audit.manager) who needs to manage audit and other GRC functions should also have sn_grc.manager (A) for cross-GRC management capabilities, and sn_audit.user (B) for performing audit tasks. The sn_grc.user (C) and sn_grc.reader (D) roles provide lesser access than needed for managing. There is no sn_grc.developer role (E).

questions.stem: What table extends from Document Table?
questions.explanation: The Document table (sn_grc_document) is extended by Policy (sn_compliance_policy), Authority Document (sn_compliance_authority_document), and Risk Framework (sn_risk_framework). Risk (A) extends Item. Risk Response Task (C) extends Task. Risk Statement (D) — also known as Risk Definition — extends Content. Of the options, Risk Framework (B) extends Document.

questions.stem: Which of the following are scoped applications related to the Risk and Compliance applications? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: The core GRC scoped applications include: GRC: Profiles (A) — foundational entities/tables, GRC: UCF Compliance (C) — Unified Compliance Framework integration, GRC: Policy and Compliance (D) — policies/controls, and GRC: Risk Management (F) — risk register/scoring. GRC: Attestation Design (B) exists but is less commonly listed as a core R&C app. GRC: Performance Analytics (E) is a plugin, not a standalone scoped application.

questions.stem: Which tables extend the Content (sn_grc_content) table? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The Content table (sn_grc_content) is extended by Citation (sn_compliance_citation, option A) and Control Objective/Policy Statement (sn_compliance_policy_statement, option C). Also extended by Risk Statement/Risk Definition (sn_risk_definition). Issue (B) has its own table. Risk (D) extends Item, not Content.

questions.stem: All of the following are PARENT tables which exist within the GRC Entities application scope EXCEPT.
questions.explanation: The three parent tables in the GRC framework are Document (sn_grc_document), Item (sn_grc_item), and Content (sn_grc_content). Indicator (D) is a separate table (sn_grc_indicator) within the GRC Profiles scope but is NOT one of the three primary parent tables. It tracks compliance monitoring results rather than serving as a parent for GRC record types.

questions.stem: Which table stored the links from Entity to Entity Types?
questions.explanation: The many-to-many relationship between Entities (profiles) and Entity Types (profile types) is stored in sn_grc_m2m_profile_profile_type (D). This table is in the GRC: Profiles scope (sn_grc prefix). Options A uses sn_compliance prefix (wrong scope), B links risks to profiles, and C links policies to profiles.

questions.stem: Where does a policy get published to when it is approved?
questions.explanation: When a policy is approved and published in ServiceNow GRC, it gets published to the Knowledge Base (D). This makes policies accessible to the broader organization through the Knowledge Base or Service Portal. The other options (Knowledge Summit, ServiceNow Library, Authoritative Records) are not valid publication targets for GRC policies.

questions.stem: What GRC module would you access in order to update Entity Types?
questions.explanation: Entity Types are managed under the Scoping module in GRC applications. The navigation path is Policy and Compliance > Scoping > Entity Types (or Risk > Scoping > Entity Types, or Audit > Scoping > Entity Types). Risk > Entities (A) shows entity records, not entity types. Scoping > Profiles (B) uses old terminology. CMDB (D) is unrelated to GRC entity types.

questions.stem: The ServiceNow Platform requires which external components in order to ingest data from other systems?

options.text: The platform includes an SDK template that allows developers to enhance it using Java
A messaging bus needs to be developed
The platform allows XML to be ingested, and it required developers to leverage XSLT to map it properly
The platform has Integration Service that allow users and developers to ingest data from a variety of sources

questions.explanation: The ServiceNow platform includes Integration Services (IntegrationHub, REST/SOAP APIs, Import Sets, etc.) that allow users and developers to ingest data from various external sources without needing custom development. It doesn't require an SDK with Java (A), a custom messaging bus (B), or manual XSLT mapping (C). The platform natively handles data ingestion from multiple formats and protocols.

questions.stem: You are working with your customer to determine necessary audit management workflow configurations. What should they know about the approval process for audit engagements? (Choose three.)

options.text: If the engagement is approved and there are remaining open tasks or issues, it automatically moves into the Follow Up state.
If the engagement is approved and there are no remaining open tasks or issues, it automatically moves into the Closed state.
If the engagement is rejected, it automatically moves back to the Fieldwork state.
If the engagement is approved and there are remaining open tasks or issues, it automatically moves into the Fieldwork state.
If the engagement is rejected, it automatically moves into the Scope state.

questions.explanation: The audit engagement approval workflow operates as follows: If approved with remaining open tasks/issues, it moves to Follow Up (A). If approved with no remaining tasks/issues, it moves to Closed (B). If rejected, it moves back to Fieldwork (C). Option D (approved → Fieldwork) is incorrect — approved engagements go to Follow Up or Closed. Option E (rejected → Scope) is wrong — rejected goes to Fieldwork.

questions.stem: Which GRC application would you use to manage internal or external consultancy processes that aim to prove the effectiveness of controls?
questions.explanation: Audit Management (A) is the GRC application used to manage internal or external audit consultancy processes aimed at proving the effectiveness of controls. It handles audit engagements, control testing, interviews, walkthroughs, and findings. Risk Management (B) handles risk identification/scoring. Vendor Risk Management (C) handles third-party risk. Policy and Compliance (D) manages policies and compliance monitoring.

questions.stem: What are the Risk Scoring methods available in ServiceNow? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: ServiceNow provides two risk scoring methods: Quantitative (A) and Qualitative (B). Quantitative uses numerical values (SLE, ARO, ALE). Qualitative uses descriptive scales (Impact and Likelihood ratings). Inherent (C), Residual (D), and Calculated (E) are risk score types, not scoring methods — they represent different stages of risk evaluation within either method.

questions.stem: The Risk thresholds in the Risk Criteria Matrix (default values) do not line up with company needs. What should you do?

options.text: Configure the Risk Criteria in ServiceNow
Identify Risk that will benefit from the default values
Demonstrate Risk scoring scenarios using the default values
Use the default values to determine new company approach

questions.explanation: When the default Risk Criteria Matrix values don't align with company needs, you should configure the Risk Criteria in ServiceNow (A) to match the organization's specific thresholds. The Risk Criteria Matrix is fully configurable — impact levels, likelihood levels, and score thresholds can all be customized. Using default values that don't fit (B, C, D) would defeat the purpose of proper risk management.

questions.stem: Who can move a Policy into Review? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: A Policy can be moved from Draft to Review by the sys admin (A) and the policy owner (D). The policy owner is typically the person responsible for the policy content and initiates the review cycle. Sys admin has override capabilities. Policy approvers (B) act during the Awaiting Approval state. Policy reviewers (C) act during the Review state itself, not to initiate it.

questions.stem: The Citation table is a child table of which parent?
questions.explanation: The Citation table (sn_compliance_citation) extends the Content table (sn_grc_content, option A). In GRC table hierarchy, Content is the parent of Citation, Control Objective (Policy Statement), and Risk Statement (Risk Definition). Authority Document (B) extends Document. Item (C) is parent of Risk and Control. Document (D) is parent of Policy and Authority Document.

questions.stem: Control Failure Factor represents the impact of Control Failures on what score?
questions.explanation: The Control Failure Factor represents the impact of control failures on the Calculated risk score (D). The Calculated score is derived from Inherent and Residual scores, adjusted by the Control Failure Factor and Indicator Failure Factor. Inherent (A) represents risk before any controls. Residual (B) represents risk after controls. The Calculated score specifically factors in control and indicator effectiveness.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is not a trigger for issue creation?

options.text: Manual issue created by any manager or admin role as well as by audit user
Risk assessment returns the inherent and residual risk impact as ‘Very High’
Attestation returns the result as ‘Not Implemented’
Control effectiveness is ‘Ineffective’ and the state of control test is ‘Closed Complete’

questions.explanation: Issue creation triggers in GRC include: manual creation by managers/admins/audit users (A), indicator failure (B), attestation returning 'Not Implemented' (D), and control test 'Ineffective' with 'Closed Complete' state (E). A risk assessment returning high inherent/residual risk (C) is NOT an automatic trigger for issue creation — it may prompt risk response tasks but not issues.

questions.stem: GRC Options in Interactive Filters are only available through which feature?
questions.explanation: GRC options in Interactive Filters are only available through Performance Analytics (C). PA provides the dashboard and filtering capabilities that allow GRC users to create interactive visual filters on GRC data. The GRC PA content pack enables these specific filter options for risk, compliance, and audit data visualization.

questions.stem: In which state can reviewers either send the Policy back to draft or forward it by requesting approval?
questions.explanation: In the Review state (D), policy reviewers can either send the policy back to Draft for further editing or forward it by requesting approval (moving to Awaiting Approval). Review is the collaborative evaluation phase between Draft and Awaiting Approval in the policy lifecycle: Draft → Review → Awaiting Approval → Published → Retired.

questions.stem: The Risk Scoring values are entered on the Risk Statement. What records inherits the values from the Risk Statement?
questions.explanation: Risk scoring values (Impact, Likelihood, SLE, ARO) are defined on the Risk Statement (Risk Definition), and Registered Risks (C) inherit these values. When an Entity Type is scoped to a Risk Statement, each generated risk instance inherits the scoring criteria from its parent Risk Statement. Risk Criteria Matrix (A) defines thresholds. Risk Framework (B) groups risk statements. Risk Response Issues (D) track remediation.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements correctly describe the risk management lifecycle process?

options.text: Access, Identify and Plan, Control, Review
Control, Review, Assess, Identify and Plan
Identify and Plan, Assess, Control, Review
Identify and Plan, Review, Assess, Control

questions.explanation: The correct risk management lifecycle process in ServiceNow is: Identify and Plan → Assess → Control → Review (C). First you identify risks and plan the approach, then assess them (scoring), then implement controls to mitigate, then review the effectiveness. This follows the standard risk management framework progression from discovery through monitoring.

questions.stem: When calculating compliance scores, what is true about the weighting of Controls? (Choose two.)

options.text: Controls are not weighted equally by default
The weight of the Control is set when the Control is created

questions.explanation: When calculating compliance scores, the default weight value for controls is 10 (C), and this weight is set when the Control is created (D). Controls are weighted equally by default since they all start with weight 10 (making A incorrect — they ARE weighted equally by default). The weight CAN be changed (B is wrong), allowing administrators to give more importance to certain controls in the compliance score calculation.

questions.stem: Which role(s) has the capability to create Policies? Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Policies can be created by the Compliance Manager (A) and Compliance User (C) roles. Both sn_compliance.manager and sn_compliance.user have the ability to create policy records. Compliance Admin (B) is not a standard GRC role name. Risk Manager (D) manages risks, not policies. The compliance-specific roles are needed for policy creation.

questions.stem: The ‘Add to Update Set’ utility is available for download via:
questions.explanation: The 'Add to Update Set' utility is available for download from the ServiceNow Developer site (A). This utility helps capture configuration changes into update sets for migration between instances. It's not available from the ServiceNow Store (B, which hosts applications), Community (C, which hosts discussions), or HI Support (D, which handles support cases).

questions.stem: What are the four values leveraged for the Inherent and Residual Risk Score Types?
questions.explanation: The four values used for both Inherent and Residual risk score types are: Impact, Likelihood, SLE (Single Loss Expectancy), and ARO (Annualized Rate of Occurrence) — option D. Impact and Likelihood are the qualitative components; SLE and ARO are the quantitative components. ALE (Annualized Loss Expectancy) is calculated from SLE × ARO, not entered directly. Score (C) is computed, not input.

questions.stem: What would you leverage in order to provide users with an alternate user experience to view policies, create policy exceptions, and search for controls?
questions.explanation: Service Portal (D) provides an alternate user experience where end users can view published policies, create policy exceptions, and search for controls in a consumer-friendly interface. It offers a simplified, modern UI compared to the standard platform interface. Help Desk Portal (A), Catalog Portal (B), and Access Portal (C) are not the standard GRC-facing portals.

questions.stem: What type of customers may you encounter? (Choose three.)

options.text: Organization recently acquired and had some bad audit findings (using ServiceNow GRC to help restart their process)
Organization with little to nothing in place already (implementing one or more core ServiceNow GRC applications)
Organization undergoing a full GRC transformation (implementing all three core ServiceNow GRC applications at once or in a phased approach)
Organization implementing ServiceNow GRC to help ease their Customer Service organization (using other tools to manage other processes)
Organization implementing ServiceNow GRC to help ease their Help Desk organization (using other tools to manage other processes)

questions.explanation: The three types of GRC customers commonly encountered are: organizations recently acquired with bad audit findings needing to restart their GRC process (A), organizations with little in place implementing one or more core GRC apps (B), and organizations undergoing full GRC transformation implementing all three core apps (C). Options D and E describe Customer Service or Help Desk scenarios, which are not GRC implementation drivers.

questions.stem:
Possible regulations when Entity scoping for Healthcare:
(Choose two.)
questions.explanation: For healthcare entity scoping, the key regulations are HITRUST (A) and HIPAA (C). HITRUST (Health Information Trust Alliance) provides a certifiable security framework. HIPAA (Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act) is the US federal regulation for protecting health information. FISMA (B) is for federal government systems. HETRUST (D) is not a real regulation.

questions.stem: For Control records, who can modify the Control in the Draft state?

options.text: Only the person assigned the Attestation

questions.explanation: In the Draft state, all compliance users (A) can modify the Control record. Draft is the initial, open editing state where broad access is granted. Once the control moves to Monitor, Attest, or Review states, more restrictive role requirements apply (e.g., only Compliance Manager or sys_admin can move to Monitor). The Draft state intentionally allows wide collaboration.

questions.stem: Control indicators may be triggered or scheduled in which state?
questions.explanation: Control indicators can be triggered or scheduled in the Monitor state (B). Monitor is the active compliance monitoring phase where indicators run to evaluate control effectiveness. In Draft (E), the control is still being configured. In Attest (D) and Review (C), the control is being evaluated or reviewed. In Retired (A), the control is no longer active.

questions.stem: Which role reviews the risk response and moves the Risk record into the Monitor state at the appropriate time?
questions.explanation: The Risk Manager (A) reviews the risk response and moves the Risk record into the Monitor state when appropriate. Risk Managers have the authority to evaluate response effectiveness and transition risks through their lifecycle states. Risk Users (B) work on assigned tasks. Risk Readers (C) have read-only access. Risk Owner (D) is not a standard GRC role name.

questions.stem: Entity scoping is used for what?

options.text: Make sure that all of your Entities have the right visibility
Create and assign controls to the correct users
Create, assign, and manage controls and risks across an enterprise
Scope out the different users and roles that have access to the platform

questions.explanation: Entity scoping is used to create, assign, and manage controls and risks across an enterprise (C). It provides a top-down, structured approach for maintaining the risk universe — the hierarchical library of risks and controls mapped to organizational entities. It goes beyond just visibility (A), user assignment (B), or access management (D). Entity scoping is the core mechanism for enterprise-wide risk and control governance.

questions.stem: The SOX content pack includes a series of policies, control, risks. How are all of these components linked together?
questions.explanation: The SOX content pack includes pre-built policies, controls, and risks that are all automatically linked together (C). When installed from the ServiceNow Store, the relationships between policies, control objectives, citations, and risk statements are pre-configured. No mapping file (A), manual linking (B), or batch import (D) is required — the content pack handles all associations automatically.

questions.stem:
UCF has a collection of what? Select all UCF terms.
(Choose three.)
questions.explanation: UCF (Unified Compliance Framework) uses these key terms: Authority Documents (B), Citations (D), and Controls (E). In UCF terminology, Authority Documents are the regulatory sources, Citations are specific requirements from those documents, and Controls (Common Controls) are the compliance measures. Control Indicators (A) and Policies (C) are ServiceNow GRC terms, not UCF-specific terminology.

questions.stem: As a customer reaches greater GRC maturity, what can we expect to see occurring across their organization? (Choose three.)

options.text: Single Risk and Control frameworks across enterprise available to all stakeholders
Reliance on spreadsheet management for risk reporting
Continuous real-time monitoring of control performance

questions.explanation: As organizations reach greater GRC maturity, they exhibit: a single risk and control framework available enterprise-wide to all stakeholders (A), continuous real-time monitoring of control performance (C), and cross-functional process automation (D). Mature organizations move AWAY from spreadsheet management (B is wrong) and adopt proactive rather than reactive strategies (E is wrong).

questions.stem: Which scheduled jobs in the GRC: Profiles scope help manage the population of Entity records? (Choose two.)

options.text: GRC Entity and Risk Statement Data Collection

questions.explanation: Two key scheduled jobs in the GRC: Profiles scope help manage Entity records: the GRC indicator nightly run (A) processes indicators for entity monitoring, and GRC Profile Generation (C) generates entity records based on entity type filters. GRC Entity and Risk Statement Data Collection (B) and GRC Refresh Risk Scores (D) are related to risk management, not the Profiles scope entity population.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the correct statement about Risk Scoring formulas?
questions.explanation: The correct quantitative risk scoring formula is SLE x ARO = ALE (A). Single Loss Expectancy multiplied by Annualized Rate of Occurrence equals the Annualized Loss Expectancy. This is a standard risk quantification formula. The other options have incorrect formula combinations — ALE is always calculated from SLE and ARO, not the reverse.

questions.stem: For classic risk assessment, while a Risk is in the Assess state, reviewers can do which of the following? (Choose two.)

options.text: Answer the assessment, moving the Risk to Respond
Set the Risk back to Draft

questions.explanation: In the Assess state during classic risk assessment, reviewers can answer the assessment to move the risk to Respond (A) and set the risk back to Draft (D). They cannot move the risk directly to Monitor (B) — that happens after the Respond state. Deleting a risk (C) is not a standard option during assessment. The Assess state is for evaluation before response planning.

questions.stem: What is the condition that must exist to edit the factor guidance of a published risk assessment methodology (RAM)?

options.text: All assessment instance records are in the Monitor state
All assessment instance records are closed
All assessment instance records are deleted
States of the assessment instance records are irrelevant
All assessment instance records are canceled

questions.explanation: To edit the factor guidance of a published RAM, all assessment instance records must be deleted (C). This is a strict requirement because factor guidance changes would invalidate existing assessment responses. Having instances in Monitor state (A), closed (B), or canceled (E) is not sufficient. The records must be fully deleted, not just in a terminal state. States being irrelevant (D) is incorrect.

questions.stem: Policies can be automatically published after which of the following occurs?

options.text: Related control objectives are marked active
Policy is approved by all approvers
Policy is approved by one approver

questions.explanation: Policies can be automatically published after they are approved by all approvers (C). Once every designated approver has given approval, the policy workflow transitions from Awaiting Approval to Published state automatically. A single approver (D) is not sufficient — all must approve. Control objective activation (A) and policy exception closure (B) don't trigger policy publication.

questions.stem: To allow other applications to request a policy exception, you must complete the integration registry form. In addition to providing the name of the registry entry, what additional information is needed to complete the form?

options.text: You must indicate the audience for requesting policy exceptions
You must indicate the intended Service Portal
You must indicate the policy exception target table
You must indicate the allowed policy acknowledgement campaigns

questions.explanation: When completing the integration registry form to allow other applications to request policy exceptions, you must indicate the policy exception target table (C) — this defines where the exception request will be created. The audience (A), Service Portal (B), and acknowledgement campaigns (D) are not part of the integration registry form requirements for cross-application policy exception requests.

questions.stem: The overall goal of Entity Classes is to:

options.text: To enable reporting and to support advanced risk assessment
Show relationships between Entities and policies and map them directly to Citations
Associate Control Objectives and Risk Statements with Risks and Controls
To provide specific information about an Entity, such as who owns the Entity

questions.explanation: The overall goal of Entity Classes is to enable reporting and to support advanced risk assessment (A). Entity Classes group entities into logical categories for aggregate reporting and are required for leveraging advanced risk assessments with entity-based context. They don't map policies to citations (B), associate control objectives with risks (C — that's entity types), or provide entity ownership details (D).

questions.stem: What is the minimum role required for creating a policy acknowledgement campaign?
questions.explanation: The minimum role required to create a policy acknowledgement campaign is sn_compliance.user (B). Compliance users have sufficient permissions to configure and launch acknowledgement campaigns targeting specific user audiences. Higher roles like sn_compliance.admin (C) and sn_compliance.manager (D) also have this capability but aren't the minimum. Risk roles (A) and control owner (E) don't manage policy acknowledgements.

questions.stem: Which of the following are the classic risk score types that ServiceNow tracks? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The three classic risk score types in ServiceNow are: Inherent (B, risk before controls), Residual (A, risk after controls are applied), and Calculated (C, adjusted score using Control and Indicator Failure Factors). Operational (D) and Digital (E) are categories of risk, not score types within the classic risk scoring framework.

questions.stem: What is the condition that must exist to edit the risk scoring logic of a published risk assessment methodology (RAM)?

options.text: All assessment instance records are closed
All assessment instance records are deleted or canceled
All assessment instance records are in the Monitor state
All assessment instance records are in the Draft state

questions.explanation: To edit the risk scoring logic of a published RAM, all assessment instance records must be deleted or canceled (B). Unlike factor guidance (which requires deletion only), the scoring logic can be modified when instances are either deleted or canceled — both terminal states that prevent scoring inconsistencies. Having instances in Monitor (C) or Draft (D) state is insufficient. Simply being closed (A) is not enough.

questions.stem: Which of the following extends from Document Table? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The Document table (sn_grc_document) is extended by Policy (sn_compliance_policy, option B) and Authority Document (sn_compliance_authority_document, option D). Also extended by Risk Framework. Citation (A) extends Content, not Document. Control Objective (C) also extends Content (as sn_compliance_policy_statement). Only Policy and Authority Document extend from Document.

questions.stem: What is the minimum role required to create a risk assessment methodology (RAM)?
questions.explanation: The minimum role required to create a Risk Assessment Methodology (RAM) is sn_risk.admin (D). RAM creation is an administrative configuration task that requires the risk admin role. sn_risk.manager (C) can initiate assessments using RAMs but cannot create them. sn_risk.user (B) has basic risk access. sn_compliance.admin (A) is for compliance, not risk assessment methodology management.

questions.stem: Which table stores the links from Policy to Control Objective?
questions.explanation: The many-to-many relationship between Policy and Control Objective (Policy Statement) is stored in sn_compliance_m2m_policy_statement (C). This table links policies to their associated control objectives. Option A links policies to entity types, B links policies to entities, and D links control objectives to entity types.

questions.stem: What is a risk register?
questions.explanation: A risk register is a repository for all identified risks (D). It serves as the central catalog of risks that have been recognized and documented, including their assessments, scores, owners, and treatment plans. It does not store unidentified risks (A), risk frameworks (B), risk statements (C), or risk criteria (E). The risk register is the operational tracking system for known risks.

questions.stem: Which feature would you use to track completion of certain tasks?
questions.explanation: SLAs (Service Level Agreements) are used to track completion of certain tasks within specified timeframes (B). SLAs define expected completion times and trigger alerts/escalations when deadlines approach or are missed. Related Lists (A) display related records. Workflow Editor (C) designs process flows. Notifications (D) send alerts but don't inherently track completion time.

questions.stem: Which GRC application would you use to determine where the organization is the most vulnerable or has the most exposure?
questions.explanation: Risk Management (D) is the GRC application used to determine where the organization is most vulnerable or has the most exposure. It provides risk identification, assessment, scoring, and visualization across the enterprise. Vendor Risk Management (A) focuses on third-party risks. Audit Management (B) verifies control effectiveness. Policy and Compliance (C) manages regulatory adherence.

questions.stem: What are the terms for level of risk before and after any actions are taken? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Inherent risk (C) is the level of risk before any controls or actions are taken — the raw, unmitigated risk. Residual risk (E) is the level of risk remaining after controls and mitigation actions have been applied. Operational (A) and Digital (B) are risk categories, not before/after terms. Calculated (D) is a score type using failure factors. Solutioned (F) is not a standard risk term.

questions.stem: What types of tasks are specific to the Audit module? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: The four task types specific to the Audit module are: Interview (B), Walkthrough (C), Control Test (D), and Activity (E). These are created as part of audit engagements during the Fieldwork phase. Control Attestation (A) belongs to the Compliance module, not Audit. Remediation (F) is for issues, not a specific audit task type.

questions.stem: What baseline criteria determine when notifications are triggered in relation to audit tasks? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The baseline criteria that trigger notifications for audit tasks are Expiration (A) and Reassignment (C). When an audit task approaches or passes its due date, expiration notifications are sent. When a task is reassigned to a different user, reassignment notifications are triggered. Percentage completion (B), and due date changes (D) are not baseline notification triggers for audit tasks.

questions.stem: What minimum role is needed to bulk initiate risk assessments using the risk assessment scheduler?
questions.explanation: The minimum role required to bulk initiate risk assessments using the risk assessment scheduler is sn_risk.manager (D). Risk managers can schedule and initiate assessments across multiple entities. sn_risk.admin creates RAMs but the scheduler requires the manager role. sn_risk.user (B) has basic access. sn_grc.business_user (A) is a lighter role without scheduler access.

questions.stem: Common controls from UCF import into which table in ServiceNow?
questions.explanation: UCF Common Controls import into the Control Objective table (sn_compliance_policy_statement, option B). In UCF terminology, 'Common Controls' map to ServiceNow GRC 'Control Objectives'. The UCF integration documentation specifies this terminology mapping: UCF Common Controls → GRC Control Objectives. They don't import into Policy (A), Policy Exception (C), or Authority Document (D) tables.

questions.stem: An Entity can belong to one or multiple of which of the following?
questions.explanation: An Entity can belong to one or multiple Entity Types (A). Entity Types define the grouping criteria for entities — for example, an entity could be both a 'Data Center' entity type and a 'Critical Infrastructure' entity type simultaneously. The m2m table sn_grc_m2m_profile_profile_type supports this many-to-many relationship. Options B, C, D don't describe the primary organizational structure for entities.

questions.stem: When reviewing the Control Objective Table form with your customer, what are the most common choice lists to be configured? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The most common choice lists configured on the Control Objective form are Classification (B), Category (C), and Type (D). These choice fields allow customers to categorize and classify their control objectives for filtering and reporting. Reference (A) is a field type, not a typical choice list to configure. Description (E) is a text field, not a choice list.

questions.stem: Which ServiceNow roles can manually move a Control record into the Monitor state? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The System admin (B) and Compliance manager (D) can manually move a Control record into the Monitor state. These roles have elevated permissions to transition controls through their lifecycle. Control owners (A) typically work within the control but may not have the authority to change states. Process owners (C) is not a standard GRC role for this action.

questions.stem: For classic risk assessment, what are the risk components that apply to the Qualitative method? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The Qualitative risk scoring method uses Impact (C) and Likelihood (D) as its two components. These are descriptive/categorical scales (e.g., Low/Medium/High/Critical). SLE (A) and ARO (B) are components of the Quantitative method, which uses numerical monetary values. The Qualitative method evaluates risk through subjective assessment of potential impact severity and probability.

questions.stem: On which records is the entity a required field? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Entity is a required field on Risk (A) and Control (B) records. Every registered risk and control must be associated with an entity, which identifies the organizational unit, system, or process they apply to. Policy (C) is a document-level record not requiring an entity. Control Objective (D) and Risk Statement (E) are content-level records that scope to Entity Types, not individual entities.

questions.stem: Entity Types are applied to which types of records? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Entity Types are applied to Risk Statements (A), Control Objectives (D), and Policies (E). When scoped to a Risk Statement, entities auto-generate risks. When scoped to a Control Objective, entities auto-generate controls. Policies can also be associated with entity types. Issues (B), Risks (C), and Controls (F) are the generated records from this scoping — they receive entities, not entity types directly.

questions.stem: What new related list was added to the risk statement and entity records after migrating to advanced risk assessment?
questions.explanation: After migrating to Advanced Risk Assessment, the Aggregated risk related list (A) is added to risk statement and entity records. This list shows rolled-up risk scores across the hierarchy, enabling bottom-up risk aggregation. Risk assessments (B) and assessment instances (D) are related but not the new addition. Risk tolerance (C) is configured at the methodology level, not as a new related list on these records.

questions.stem: What ensures that every time you create an Entity from a specific table, the Class of the Entity is set according to the rule?
questions.explanation: Entity Class Rules (A) ensure that every time you create an entity from a specific table, the class is set automatically according to the rule. These rules match entity creation from specific source tables (e.g., cmn_location) and assign the appropriate entity class. Entity business rules (B) are generic platform rules. Entity class assignment (C) and entity type rules (D) are not the specific mechanism for auto-setting classes.

questions.stem: The consolidated assessment feature can be used on which of the following? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The consolidated assessment feature can be used on classic risk assessments (B) and control attestations (D). This feature allows assessors to respond to grouped assessments — providing the same response for all or different responses for each. Control tests (A) involve specific testing procedures. Issues (C) are findings/problems, not assessments that can be consolidated.

questions.stem: Which table stores the links from the Entity Type to Risk Statement?
questions.explanation: The table storing links from Entity Type to Risk Statement is sn_risk_m2m_risk_definition_profile_type (C). 'risk_definition' is the technical name for Risk Statement, and 'profile_type' is the technical name for Entity Type. Option A uses 'statement' instead of 'risk_definition'. Option B links frameworks to entity types. Option D links policies (wrong scope).

questions.stem: For classic risk assessment, indicator failure factor represents the impact of risk indicator failures on what score?
questions.explanation: In classic risk assessment, the Indicator Failure Factor represents the impact of risk indicator failures on the Calculated ALE (B). The Calculated score combines Inherent and Residual data with adjustment factors — the Indicator Failure Factor adjusts the ALE calculation based on how indicators are performing. Inherent ALE (A, D) is not adjusted by indicator failures. Residual ALE (C) reflects risk after controls.

questions.stem: Praveen is a Risk Manager. Why would he want to utilize Entity Types and Entities? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: A Risk Manager like Praveen would use Entity Types and Entities to: monitor risk exposure across enterprise entities (A), perform risk assessments on entities (C), and perform risk reporting by entity (E). Remediating vulnerabilities (B) is a security operations task, not a core Entity Type use. Policy exceptions (D) are compliance-specific, not directly tied to entity type/entity usage for risk managers.

questions.stem: If you create a control manually and later decide to create them automatically, what will be the result?

options.text: ServiceNow will delete the manually created control
ServiceNow creates a duplicate control and notifies the control owner
ServiceNow creates a duplicate control without notifying the control owner
ServiceNow identifies the control and does not create a duplicate

questions.explanation: If you manually create a control and later enable automatic creation, ServiceNow creates a duplicate control without notifying the control owner (C). The platform does not detect or reconcile manually created controls with auto-generated ones. It won't delete the manual control (A), won't notify about duplicates (B), and does not identify existing controls to prevent duplication (D). This is a known consideration when switching creation methods.

questions.stem: Which of the following records does not have a lifecycle?
questions.explanation: Control Objectives (A) do not have a lifecycle — they are either active or inactive. Policies (B) have a full lifecycle: Draft → Review → Awaiting Approval → Published → Retired. Policy Exceptions (C) have approval and expiration states. Controls (D) have a lifecycle: Draft → Monitor → Attest → Review. Control Objectives serve as templates/definitions and don't transition through states.

questions.stem: Which of the following relationship sets are considered a many-to-many relationship? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The many-to-many relationships in GRC are: Control and Risk (C) — controls mitigate multiple risks and vice versa, Control Objective and Entity Type (D) — scoping multiple entity types to multiple control objectives, and Entity Type and Entity (E) — entities can belong to multiple entity types. Entity Type and Entity Class (A) have no direct m2m relationship. Indicator Template and Entity Type (B) is typically a one-to-many assignment.

questions.stem: How can you get the SOX content pack?
questions.explanation: The SOX content pack is available from the ServiceNow Store (A). It can be downloaded and installed as an application package containing pre-built SOX policies, control objectives, citations, and risk statements. It's not delivered through patch updates (B), platform upgrades (C), or professional services (D) — it's a separately installable store application.

questions.stem: Critical parts of a successful GRC implementation are understanding the customers current: (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Critical parts of a successful GRC implementation include understanding the customer's current: regulatory requirements (A), risk and compliance personas (B), and GRC processes (C). These foundational elements determine how to configure the platform effectively. Data breaches (D) and audit failures (E) are events/outcomes that may motivate GRC adoption but aren't implementation requirements to understand in the same way.

questions.stem: Which of the following are ServiceNow classic risk score types? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The three classic risk score types in ServiceNow are: Calculated (B), Inherent (C), and Residual (E). Inherent represents risk before controls, Residual represents risk after controls, and Calculated adjusts scores using Control and Indicator Failure Factors. Applied (A) and Generated (D) are not valid risk score types in the ServiceNow GRC framework.

questions.stem: A control objective has been related to a risk statement and they've been scoped with the same entity type. What can we expect to occur?

options.text: Risks for this risk statement will be moved back into a Review state since there are new factors impacting risk likelihood.
A control for this control objective, with a matching entity, will be related to the registered risk for this risk statement as a mitigating control.
The control objective will be marked as compliant since it is mitigating the related risk statement.
Risk scores will automatically decrease for the risk statement's risks since there are now mitigating controls.

questions.explanation: When a Control Objective and Risk Statement are scoped with the same Entity Type, a control for that control objective with a matching entity will be related to the registered risk for that risk statement as a mitigating control (B). This automatic relationship is a key benefit of entity scoping — it links controls to risks they mitigate. Options A, C, D describe incorrect consequences.

questions.stem: Santa Clara Facility and Boston Facility are examples of what?
questions.explanation: Santa Clara Facility and Boston Facility are examples of Entities (A) — specific organizational items being tracked for risk and compliance. They are individual records (facilities) that would belong to an Entity Type like 'Facilities' or 'Data Centers.' Entity Objects (B) are the source table records. Entity Class (C) is a grouping of entities. Entity Type (D) defines the category, not individual locations.

questions.stem: Which collection of tables extend the Item (sn_grc_item) table? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The Item table (sn_grc_item) is extended by Risk (sn_risk_risk, option A) and Control (sn_compliance_control, option D). These are the two primary GRC records that track specific risk instances and control implementations. Citation (B) extends Content. Policy (C) extends Document. Item is specifically the parent for operational GRC records that are scoped to entities.

questions.stem: Who should be directly involved in GRC implementations? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: People directly involved in GRC implementations include: ServiceNow platform experts (C) for technical configuration, Business Analysts (D) for process mapping, Risk and compliance experts (E) for domain knowledge, and CMDB process owner (F) for data governance alignment. Board of directors (A) and Chief Executive (B) are sponsors/stakeholders but not directly involved in implementation work.

questions.stem: Which of the following are triggers for automatic creation of an issue? (Choose two.)

options.text: Indicator result is Failed or Not Passed
Control tests have been assigned but not tested

questions.explanation: The automatic triggers for issue creation are: Attestation result is 'Not Implemented' (A) and Indicator result is 'Failed' or 'Not Passed' (B). These conditions indicate compliance failures that require remediation. Policy Exception not approved (C) results in the exception being denied, not an issue. Control tests assigned but not tested (D) is a status tracking concern, not an automatic issue trigger.

questions.stem: Risk criteria typically include definitions of different levels of what? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Risk criteria typically include definitions of different levels of Impact (A) and Likelihood (B). These two dimensions form the basis of risk assessment in the Risk Criteria Matrix — Impact defines severity levels (e.g., Negligible to Catastrophic) and Likelihood defines probability levels (e.g., Rare to Almost Certain). Criticality (C), Importance (D), and Priority (E) are not standard risk criteria dimensions.

questions.stem: Which is not a type of key compliance indicator?
questions.explanation: Reference (D) is not a type of key compliance indicator. The valid compliance indicator types are: Performance Analytics (A) for PA-driven indicators, Manual (B) for user-entered results, Scripted (C) for script-based evaluation, and Basic (E) for condition-based monitoring. Reference is a field type used in forms but not a compliance indicator type.

questions.stem: The Entity Type table has a many-to-many relationship with which tables? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The Entity Type table has many-to-many relationships with Risk Statement (A) and Policy (B). Entity Types are scoped to Risk Statements to auto-generate risks and to Policies for compliance tracking. The m2m tables are sn_risk_m2m_risk_definition_profile_type and sn_compliance_m2m_policy_profile_type. Control (C) and Risk (D) are Item-level records that relate to individual entities, not entity types via m2m.

questions.stem: Unified Compliance Framework (UCF) uses a slightly different nomenclature structure than ServiceNow. Common controls from UCF import into which table in ServiceNow?
questions.explanation: UCF Common Controls import into the Control Objective table (sn_compliance_policy_statement, option A). The UCF-to-GRC terminology mapping is: UCF Common Controls = ServiceNow Control Objectives, UCF Authority Documents = ServiceNow Authority Documents, UCF Citations = ServiceNow Citations. The control objective table stores these mapped UCF controls, not the Control, Citation, or Authority Document tables.

questions.stem: What dependency modeling feature can be used in the Classic UI to build relationships between Entity Classes?
questions.explanation: The GRC Workbench (A) is the dependency modeling feature in the Classic UI that allows customers to build relationships between Entity Classes and visualize upstream/downstream dependencies. It provides a graphical interface for creating and managing entity relationships. Options B, C, D are not valid GRC feature names for dependency modeling.

questions.stem: The content table (sn_grcs_content) is a parent table of:
questions.explanation: The Content table (sn_grc_content) is a parent table of sn_risk_definition (C), which is the Risk Statement/Risk Definition table. Content is also parent to Citation (sn_compliance_citation) and Control Objective (sn_compliance_policy_statement). sn_grc_profile (A) is the Entity table in GRC Profiles scope. sn_risk_framework (B) extends Document, not Content. sn_risk_risk (D) extends Item, not Content.

questions.stem: Which of the following roles can create a policy? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Policies can be created by the Compliance User (B, sn_compliance.user) and Compliance Manager (C, sn_compliance.manager) roles. Both roles have the permissions needed to create policy records. Audit User (A) works within audit management. Risk User (D) works with risk records. Compliance Reader (E) has read-only access and cannot create policies.

questions.stem: Which filter navigation syntax displays the default form view of the Risk table in the Content Frame?
questions.explanation: The syntax sn_risk_risk.form (A) displays the default form view of the Risk table in the Content Frame. The .form suffix (lowercase) opens the form view within the standard content area. .LIST (B, all caps) opens a list in a new tab. .FORM (C, all caps) would open the form in a separate tab. .list (D, lowercase) shows the list view in the content frame, not the form view.

questions.stem: What three records need to be set-up when integrating with a provider RSS feed? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Setting up a Regulatory Change Management provider RSS feed requires three records: a Feed sources record (A) defining the RSS source, a Provider record (B) identifying the regulatory body, and a Connection and Credentials record (D) for authentication. The Regulatory Feed record (C) is the result, not a setup record. Regulatory Change Tasks (E) are created after feed processing, not during setup.

questions.stem: Which of the following are Policy Lifecycle states included in the ServiceNow baseline? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The baseline Policy lifecycle states include Review (B) and Published (D). The full baseline lifecycle is: Draft → Review → Awaiting Approval → Published → Retired. Expired (A), Acknowledged (C), and Verified (E) are not standard policy lifecycle states in the ServiceNow GRC baseline. These could be custom states but aren't part of the out-of-box configuration.

questions.stem: Which of the following extends from Content Table? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The Content table (sn_grc_content) is extended by Citation (sn_compliance_citation, option A) and Control Objective (sn_compliance_policy_statement, option C). Also extended by Risk Statement (sn_risk_definition). Policy (B) extends the Document table. Authority Document (D) also extends the Document table. Content serves as the parent for compliance requirements and risk definitions.

questions.stem: Which tables extend from the Task table? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Risk Response Task (B, sn_risk_m2m_risk_response_task) and Risk Event (D) extend from the Task table. The Task table is the platform parent for actionable work items. Risk Framework (A) extends Document. Risk Statement (C) extends Content. Risk (E) extends Item. Only task-oriented records like Risk Response Tasks and Risk Events extend from the Task table.

questions.stem: What are some of the drivers for customers to get the GRC suite of applications? (Choose four.)

options.text: They would like automated customer service
They would like workflow driven processes

questions.explanation: Key drivers for adopting the GRC suite include: efficiency (A) — automating manual processes, integrated reporting (B) — cross-functional visibility, transparency (C) — clear audit trails and stakeholder visibility, and workflow-driven processes (F) — automated policy/risk/audit workflows. Automated customer service (D) and custom websites (E) are not GRC suite use cases.

questions.stem: The Calculated Risk Score utilizes data from the Inherent and Residual Risk scores to determine an adjusted ALE and Score. What other data drives the adjustments?
questions.explanation: The Calculated Risk Score uses Inherent and Residual scores plus Control and Indicator Failure Factors (D) to determine the adjusted ALE and Score. Control Failure Factor represents the impact of failing controls, and Indicator Failure Factor represents the impact of failing risk indicators. Audit Scores (A), Attestation Scores (B), and Configuration Test Scores (C) don't directly feed into the Calculated Risk Score formula.

questions.stem: The advanced planning capability enables integration of Advanced Audit with PPM. If the advanced planning capability is selected when the audit plan is created, what extra related lists display on the engagement record in addition to the related lists displayed with basic planning? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: When the advanced planning capability is selected during audit plan creation, three extra related lists appear on the engagement record: Time card (A) for tracking time spent, Resource plan (B) for assigning audit resources, and Cost plan (D) for budgeting. These integrate Audit Management with PPM capabilities. Entities (C) and Milestones (E) are not the additional related lists specific to advanced planning.

questions.stem: Which of the following roles can create issues? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Issues can be created by Compliance User (D, sn_compliance.user), Audit User (E, sn_audit.user), and Risk Manager (F, sn_risk.manager) roles. These roles have the authority to document findings that require remediation. Risk Reader (A) and Compliance Reader (B) have read-only access. External Auditor (C) has limited view/task access and typically cannot create issues directly.

questions.stem: What would you use in order to accommodate a customer’s unique process around policy approvals? For example, each policy needs a second layer of approval.

options.text: Create a new field and create notifications
Add a new related list to keep track of who has already approved it and who hasn’t approved yet
Add a UI Action to track who the stakeholders are
Create a new workflow in the workflow editor

questions.explanation: To add a second layer of approval to the policy process, you should create a new workflow in the Workflow Editor (D). ServiceNow workflows allow you to define multi-stage approval chains with conditions, parallel/sequential approvals, and custom transitions. Adding fields (A), related lists (B), or UI Actions (C) don't provide the process automation needed for approval routing.

questions.stem: Which of the following are a part of the GRC: Advanced Risk scope? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The GRC: Advanced Risk application scope includes Risk Hierarchy (A) for rolled-up risk visualization and Risk Assessment Methodologies (B, sn_risk_advanced_risk_assessment_methodology) for configurable assessment processes. Risk Criteria Matrix (C) is part of classic Risk Management. Risk Framework (D) is part of the base Risk Management scope, not the Advanced Risk scope.

questions.stem: Where does one go to configure the Regulatory Change Management impact assessment template?

options.text: Impact Assessment Flow in Flow Designer

questions.explanation: The Regulatory Change Management impact assessment template is configured in the Risk Assessment Methodologies module (A). The RAM defines the assessment criteria, factors, and scoring logic used when evaluating the impact of regulatory changes. Impact Assessment Flow (B) is not a standard module. Impact Assessment Templates (C) and Risk Assessment Templates (D) are not the correct navigation paths for this configuration.

questions.stem: Service Level Agreements can be used for the which of the following? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Service Level Agreements can be applied to Risk Issues (A) and Risk Response Tasks (D) in GRC. These task-based records benefit from time-bound tracking and escalation. SLAs work on records with a lifecycle and timeline requirements. Risk (B), Risk Statement (C), and Risk Framework (E) are definition/assessment records that don't typically use SLA tracking for completion timelines.

questions.stem: Controls are generated from a Control Objective when what is applied to it?
questions.explanation: Controls are generated from a Control Objective when an Entity Type (D) is applied to it. The entity scoping process automatically creates control instances for each entity within the assigned Entity Type. Policy (A) is related to control objectives but doesn't trigger generation. Citation (B) maps regulatory requirements. Indicator templates (C) enable monitoring but don't generate controls.

questions.stem: In which state is the Policy once all approvals are received?
questions.explanation: Once all approvals are received, the Policy automatically moves to the Published state (B). The policy lifecycle flows: Draft → Review → Awaiting Approval → Published. After all designated approvers approve, the workflow transitions to Published, making the policy available to the organization through the Knowledge Base and Service Portal.

questions.stem: Setting up entity classes is required when using which GRC features? (Choose two.)

options.text: Setting up an object-based risk assessment
Adding to the policy exception integration registry
Assessing the impact of a regulatory feed

questions.explanation: Entity Classes are required when setting up object-based risk assessments (A) and leveraging advanced risk assessments (E). Advanced risk assessments use entity classes to group entities for assessment scheduling and score aggregation. Object-based assessments need entity class context. Policy exception registry (B), regulatory feed assessment (C), and classic risk assessments (D) don't require entity classes.

questions.stem: Which GRC tables serve as primary parent tables for the GRC applications? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The three primary parent tables in the GRC framework are: Content (A, sn_grc_content — parent of Citation, Control Objective, Risk Statement), Item (B, sn_grc_item — parent of Risk, Control), and Document (E, sn_grc_document — parent of Policy, Authority Document, Risk Framework). Asset (C) and Task (D) are platform tables, not GRC-specific parent tables.

questions.stem: Annualized Loss Expectancy is a feature of which risk score method?
questions.explanation: Annualized Loss Expectancy (ALE) is a feature of the Quantitative risk scoring method (B). ALE = SLE × ARO, using monetary values to express risk in financial terms. The Qualitative method (C) uses descriptive Impact and Likelihood scales without ALE. Residual (A) and Inherent (D) are risk score types, not scoring methods. ALE is exclusively associated with quantitative risk measurement.

questions.stem: For a particular risk assessment methodology (RAM), the control effectiveness score is calculated based on an individual assessment of controls. What are options for control identification? (Choose three.)

options.text: Controls are identified from library and ad-hoc
Controls are identified from indicator results
Controls are identified from related issues

questions.explanation: For a RAM's control effectiveness assessment, controls can be identified in three ways: from library and ad-hoc combined (A), from library only (C), and ad-hoc only (D). Library controls are pre-defined in the control register, while ad-hoc controls are identified during the assessment process. Controls are NOT identified from indicator results (B) or related issues (E) — those are monitoring and finding mechanisms.

questions.stem: Within the Policy Acknowledgement module, what table does the Acknowledgement Instance table extend from?

options.text: Does not extend from a table

questions.explanation: The Policy Acknowledgement Instance table does not extend from any listed table (C). It is a standalone table (sn_compliance_policy_acknowledgement_instance) that tracks individual user acknowledgement responses. It doesn't extend Task (A), Policy Acknowledgement (B), Policy (D), or Document (E). It has its own table definition to capture per-user acknowledgement records.

questions.stem:
For advanced risk assessment, risk response can be handled in the following ways:
(Choose two.)

options.text: Skipped entirely based on attributes defined in the RAM
Must create a mitigation response task
Must create at least one risk response task

questions.explanation: In advanced risk assessment, risk response can be handled by creating multiple risk response tasks (A) to address different aspects of risk treatment, or it can be skipped entirely based on attributes defined in the RAM (B). The RAM can configure whether response is mandatory or optional. Options C and D suggest rigid requirements (must create mitigation or at least one task) which don't apply — the RAM can waive response entirely.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not used to source control data for a customer’s control framework?
questions.explanation: ServiceNow Product documentation is NOT used to source control data for a customer's control framework. The three valid sources are: Customer's existing controls (B) which represent current organizational requirements, external regulatory content providers (C) like UCF or regulatory bodies, and ServiceNow content packs and accelerators (D) which provide pre-built control frameworks. Product documentation describes how the GRC application works but does not contain actual control data that would populate a customer's control framework.

questions.stem: What assessment types can be enabled when configuring a risk assessment methodology (RAM)? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: When configuring a RAM, three assessment types can be enabled: Residual Assessment (C) — evaluating risk after controls, Inherent Assessment (D) — evaluating raw risk, and Control Assessment (E) — evaluating control effectiveness. Operational (A), Application (B), and Project (F) Risk Assessment are not the three configurable assessment types within a RAM. The RAM framework uses the Inherent/Residual/Control assessment methodology.

questions.stem: How does GRC: Policy and Compliance Management track compliance to Authority Documents?

options.text: Citations are mapped to entity-scoped controls, which are tested as compliant or non-compliant.
Authority Documents are mapped to individual policies, which are either marked compliant or non-compliant.
Authority Documents are mapped to control objectives and compliance is checked when controls are tested as compliant or non-compliant.
Citations are mapped to control objectives, and compliance is checked when controls are tested as compliant or non-compliant.

questions.explanation: GRC Policy and Compliance Management tracks compliance to Authority Documents through citations mapped to control objectives, with compliance checked when controls are tested as compliant or non-compliant (D). Citations from Authority Documents link to Control Objectives, which generate Controls on entities. Control testing results (compliant/non-compliant) roll up through control objectives to determine compliance with the citations and authority documents.

questions.stem: What are some of the features of scoped applications for GRC? (Choose three.)

options.text: Requires an entitlement for all environments
All components have a namespace prefix for identification
Provides access to all global data
Ability to view all components from the sys_metadata table
Ability to restrict access to available data

questions.explanation: Key features of GRC scoped applications include: requiring an entitlement for all environments (A), all components having a namespace prefix for identification (B, e.g., sn_grc, sn_compliance, sn_risk), and ability to restrict access to available data (E). Scoped apps do NOT provide access to all global data (C) — they have restricted access by design. Viewing all components from sys_metadata (D) is a platform capability, not a scoped app feature.

questions.stem: Which of the following tables exist within the GRC: Profiles application scope? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The GRC: Profiles application scope contains: sn_grc_profile_type (A, Entity Type), sn_grc_indicator (B, Indicator), and sn_grc_profile_class (E, Entity Class). sn_grc_compliance_policy_statement (C) would be in the Compliance scope, not Profiles. sn_grc_risk_definition (D) would be in the Risk scope. The Profiles scope contains the foundational entity/profile tables with the sn_grc prefix.

questions.stem: Who can move a Policy record from Review into the next state?
questions.explanation: Any reviewer (C) can move a Policy record from Review into the next state (Awaiting Approval). During the Review phase, designated reviewers evaluate the policy and can either send it back to Draft or forward it to the approval stage. While sys admin (A) and compliance manager (B) may also have this capability, the named policy owner (D) is typically the one who initiates review, not who advances from it.

questions.stem: Which table extends from the Content Table?
questions.explanation: Risk Statement (D, also called Risk Definition, table sn_risk_definition) extends from the Content table (sn_grc_content). Risk Record (A, sn_risk_risk) extends Item. Risk Framework (B, sn_risk_framework) extends Document. Risk Response Task (C) extends Task. Among these options, only Risk Statement/Definition is a child of the Content table.

questions.stem: What happens when you assign an Entity Type to a Control Objective?

options.text: An assessment is automatically generated to test each Entity listed in the Entity Type
A policy is created automatically for every Entity listed in the Entity Type
A control is automatically generated for every Entity listed in the Entity Type
The Entity Type presents a compliance score and controls tied to it

questions.explanation: When an Entity Type is assigned to a Control Objective, a control is automatically generated for every entity listed in the Entity Type (C). This is entity scoping for compliance — each entity gets its own control instance to track compliance with that control objective. Assessments (A) are not auto-generated from this action. Policies (B) are separate document-level records. Compliance scores (D) come from control testing, not entity type assignment.

questions.stem: What are some of the baseline tables commonly leveraged in Entity filters? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Common baseline tables used in Entity filters include: Company (core_company, A) for organizational entities, Services (cmdb_ci_service, B) for IT service tracking, and Location (cmn_location, C) for geographic/facility entities. Risk (D) and Audit Engagement (E) are GRC-specific tables, not baseline platform tables used as entity filter sources. Entity filters map to existing ServiceNow tables for entity generation.

questions.stem: An external audit team needs to view all of your published policies and controls? Which role can you give the team members?
questions.explanation: The sn_audit.external_auditor (C) role is designed for external audit teams who need to view published policies and controls. This role provides appropriate read-level access for external parties without granting internal management capabilities. sn_audit_manager (A) gives too much internal authority. sn_compliance_user (B) can create/modify compliance records. sn_risk_user (D) provides risk management access that external auditors don't need.

questions.stem: An Observation can also be commonly known as what during an audit?
questions.explanation: An Observation in the context of an audit is commonly known as a Finding (D). Findings/Observations are the results of audit testing and fieldwork that document issues, exceptions, or areas of non-compliance. Evidence (A) supports findings but is different. Engagement (B) is the audit project. Problem (C) is an ITSM term, not an audit term.

questions.stem: What mapping capability in the Classic UI allows customers to relate specific Entities to each other within an Entity Class?
questions.explanation: The GRC Workbench Dependency Map (C) is the Classic UI feature that allows customers to relate specific entities to each other within an Entity Class. It provides a visual, drag-and-drop interface for creating upstream/downstream dependency relationships. Entity Class Mapper (A), Entity Workbench (B), and GRC Entity Mapper (D) are not valid ServiceNow feature names for this capability.

questions.stem: While management of a company must set the stage for all improvement efforts, which of these 5S’s is primarily driven by management?
Which feature of classic risk scoring is frequently configured by customers?
questions.explanation: The Risk Criteria Matrix (B) is the most frequently configured feature of classic risk scoring. Organizations customize the matrix to define their own impact and likelihood levels, risk score thresholds, and color-coded risk ratings that align with their risk appetite. ALE (A), Control Failure Factor (C), and Indicator Failure Factor (D) are used but less frequently customized than the Risk Criteria Matrix.

questions.stem: Which methods does ServiceNow support when migrating new policies? (Choose three.)

options.text: They can be imported from PDFs
They can be imported via an API
They can be copied from the UCF
They can be imported from Regulatory websites
They can be imported from existing spreadsheets

questions.explanation: ServiceNow supports migrating policies via API (B) using REST/SOAP web services or Import Sets, manual creation (C) directly in the platform, and importing from existing spreadsheets (F) via Import Sets or Excel upload. PDFs (A) cannot be directly imported as structured data. UCF (D) imports authority documents and controls, not policies directly. Regulatory websites (E) are not a direct import mechanism.

questions.stem: Which collection of tables extend the Document table?
questions.explanation: The Document table (sn_grc_document) is extended by Risk Framework, Policy, and Authority Document. Option C lists Risk Framework, Policy, and Authority Document — the correct set. Risk and Control (A) extend Item. Control Objective and Citation (B, D) extend Content. The Document table serves as the parent for governance-level records: frameworks, policies, and authority sources.

questions.stem: Which of the following tables are within the GRC: Policy and Compliance Management application scope? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Within the GRC: Policy and Compliance Management scope, Authority Document (A, sn_compliance_authority_document) and Policy Exception (C, sn_compliance_policy_exception) are included. These carry the sn_compliance namespace. Assessment (B) may be in a different scope. Audit Task (D, sn_audit) is in the Audit Management scope. The compliance scope specifically handles policies, authority documents, citations, control objectives, and exceptions.

questions.stem: What content can be ingested into ServiceNow as a result of the UCF integration? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The UCF integration allows ingestion of Authority Documents (C) and Citations (E) into ServiceNow. UCF provides regulatory framework content that maps to authority documents and their specific citations/requirements. Policies (A) are internally created. Risks (B) are generated from risk statements. Issues (D) are operational findings. UCF specifically delivers regulatory reference content, not operational GRC records.

questions.stem: Entity Types use Entity Filters to generate entitles based on which of the following?

options.text: Only GRC scoped tables in ServiceNow

questions.explanation: Entity Types use Entity Filters to generate entities based on any table in ServiceNow (D). The Entity Filter has a 'Table' field that can point to any table — core tables (cmn_location, core_company), CMDB tables, or even custom application tables. It's not limited to GRC scoped tables (A), core tables only (B), or third-party applications (C). Any table with records that represent organizational units can serve as an entity source.

questions.stem: A relationship between a registered risk and a control will be automatically generated when the control objective and risk statement have the same what?
