questions.explanation: A relationship between a registered risk and a control is automatically generated when the control objective and risk statement have the same Entity Type (C). When both are scoped with the same entity type, the system links the generated controls to the generated risks for matching entities. This automatic relationship creation is the core value of consistent entity scoping across risk statements and control objectives.

questions.stem: What do you select when you create a new assessment scheduler record for initiating advanced risk assessments? (Choose two.)

options.text: Entities from the designated entity type
Entities from the designated entity classes

questions.explanation: When creating a new assessment scheduler record for advanced risk assessments, you select: a published Risk Assessment Methodology/RAM (B) that defines the assessment criteria, and entities from designated entity classes (D) that define which entities to assess. You don't select any active entity (A) without classification. Entities from entity types (C) is not the scheduler's selection — it uses entity classes. ServiceNow table objects (E) are not directly selected.

questions.stem: When this property is set to true, Risk, Entity, and Risk Statement forms are impacted.

options.text: Migrate to Advanced Risk Assessments property

questions.explanation: The Migrate to Advanced Risk Assessments property (B) impacts Risk, Entity, and Risk Statement forms when set to true. This property adds advanced risk assessment fields, related lists, and functionality to these forms. The other options — Migrate to Risk Events (A), Migrate IRM enterprise (C), and Advanced Risk (D) — are either not valid property names or don't specifically affect all three form types listed.

questions.stem: Which table stores the links from Control Objective to Citation?
questions.explanation: The table storing links from Control Objective to Citation is sn_compliance_m2m_statement_citation (A, noting the typo 'cftation' in the option). This many-to-many table connects control objectives (policy statements) to citations. Option B links policies to policy statements. Option C links statements to policies (reverse). Option D links policies to entity types. The m2m_statement_citation table is the correct junction.

questions.stem: The Single Loss Expectancy is $1.000.000 and the Annual Rate of Occurrence is 20%. What is the Annualized Loss Expectancy?
questions.explanation: With SLE of $1,000,000 and ARO of 20% (0.20), the ALE = SLE x ARO = $1,000,000 x 0.20 = $200,000 (B). This is the standard quantitative risk formula where Single Loss Expectancy multiplied by Annualized Rate of Occurrence gives the expected annual financial impact. The calculation is straightforward: the probability-weighted annual expected loss.

questions.stem: What options are available when configuring the assessment context for a risk assessment methodology RAM)? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: When configuring the assessment context for a RAM, the available options are Risk (C) and Object (D). Risk context assesses risks directly, while Object context assesses arbitrary objects from ServiceNow tables. Risk Statement (A), Application Risk (B), and Project Risk (E) are not standard assessment context options in the RAM configuration. The RAM supports Risk-based and Object-based assessment contexts.

questions.stem: What are key prerequisites for a control test task to be generated?

options.text: Entity being scoped has associated controls with test plans
Entity being scoped has associated risks

questions.explanation: The key prerequisite for control test tasks to be generated is that the entity being scoped has associated controls with test plans (C). Controls must have test plans defined so the audit engagement can create test tasks. The engagement being in Scope (A) is a state, not a prerequisite. Risk assessments (B) are separate from control testing. Set frequency (D) is for indicators. Associated risks (E) doesn't directly drive test task generation.

questions.stem: Who should be directly involved in GRC implementations? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: People who should be directly involved in GRC implementations include: ServiceNow platform experts (C) for technical configuration, Risk and compliance experts (E) for domain and regulatory knowledge, and CMDB process owner (F) for data governance and entity scoping alignment. Board of directors (A) and Chief Executive (B) are executive sponsors, not directly involved in implementation. HR analysts (D) support HR processes, not GRC implementation.

questions.stem: Creating Entities in ServiceNow is easier as customers can leverage existing data used in other applications. What are some baseline tables that are commonly used to build an Entity Type? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Common baseline tables used to build Entity Types are cmn_location (A) for geographic/facility entities and core_company (B) for organizational/business unit entities. These are the most frequently used source tables for entity generation. cmn_department (C) is used less commonly. cmn_geography (D) and cmn_job_center (E) are not standard baseline tables for entity type creation. Location and Company are the primary entity sources.

questions.stem: What types of tasks are specific to the Audit module? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The three task types specific to the Audit module (from the given options of 3) are: Interview (B) — gathering information from stakeholders, Walkthrough (C) — observing process execution, and Control Test (D) — testing control effectiveness. Control Attestation (A) belongs to the Compliance module. Tabletop Exercise (E) is not a standard audit task type. Remediation (F) belongs to issue management.

questions.stem: Which Script include can be modified to change how the compliance scores roll up?
questions.explanation: The ComplianceScoreCalculator (C) script include can be modified to change how compliance scores roll up. This script contains the logic for calculating and aggregating compliance scores across controls, control objectives, policies, and authority documents. ScoreRollUp (A), ComplianceUtils (B), and AssessmentStrategy (D) are not the correct script include names for this specific compliance score calculation function.

questions.stem: What are primary tables for the GRC Advanced Risk application scope? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The primary tables in the GRC: Advanced Risk scope are sn_risk_advanced_risk_assessment_methodology (A, noting the typo in the option) and sn_risk_advanced_factor (E). These tables store RAM configurations and assessment factors. sn_risk_advanced_criteria (B, noting the typo) may exist but is less primary. sn_risk_response_task (C) is in the base Risk scope. sn_risk_advanced_definition (D) is not a primary advanced risk table.

questions.stem: Controls are automatically moved to which state from the attestation phase?
questions.explanation: Controls are automatically moved to the Review state (B) from the attestation phase. After all control attestations are completed during the Attest phase, the control lifecycle transitions to Review, where the compliance manager evaluates the attestation results. Retired (A) is the final state. Draft (C) is the initial state. Monitor (D) precedes Attest. The flow is Draft → Monitor → Attest → Review.

questions.stem: EMEA Data Centers are an example of what?
questions.explanation: EMEA Data Centers is an example of an Entity Type (D). An Entity Type defines a category of items to track — like 'Data Centers' as a group, with specific facilities as individual entities within it. Entity Objects (A) are source table records. Individual Entities (B) would be specific data centers like 'London DC'. Entity Parent (C) is not a standard GRC term. 'EMEA Data Centers' describes a type/category of entities.

questions.stem: What is the minimum role required to approve a Policy?
questions.explanation: The minimum role required to approve a Policy is sn_compliance.user (C). Compliance users who are designated as approvers can approve policies during the Awaiting Approval state. The role doesn't need to be admin (A) or manager (B) level — the compliance user role combined with being listed as an approver is sufficient. sn_grc.user (D) is a broader GRC role but not specifically for policy approval.

questions.stem: Which roles can move the control to the ‘Monitor’ state manually? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The System Administrator (D) and Compliance Manager (E) can manually move a control to the Monitor state. These elevated roles have the authority to transition controls through their lifecycle. Compliance Reader (A) has read-only access. Risk User (B) works in the Risk module. Audit User (C) works in the Audit module. Only sys_admin and sn_compliance.manager have this specific control state transition capability.

questions.stem: All of the following are tables which exist within the GRC Profiles application scope EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: sn_grc_risk (D) is not in the GRC Profiles application scope — risks are in the GRC: Risk Management scope (sn_risk_risk). The GRC Profiles scope includes: sn_grc_profile (A, Entity), sn_grc_item (B, Item), and sn_grc_profile_type (C, Entity Type). These foundational tables have the sn_grc prefix and belong to the Profiles scope. Risk records use the sn_risk prefix and belong to a different scope.

questions.stem: The compliance score calculation may be modified by changing which control factor?
questions.explanation: The compliance score calculation can be modified by changing the Control Weight (D). Each control has a weight value (default 10) that determines its relative importance in the compliance score calculation. Higher-weighted controls have more impact on the overall score. Control Height (A), Mass (B), and Velocity (C) are not real GRC control attributes — Weight is the actual configurable factor.

questions.stem: Which of the following tables are included in the GRC: Policy and Compliance Management scoped application? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Tables in the GRC: Policy and Compliance Management scope include: sn_compliance_policy (B), sn_compliance_policy_statement (D, Control Objective), and sn_compliance_citation (G). These all carry the sn_compliance namespace. sn_compliance_risk (A) is not a valid table. sn_grc_item (C) is in the Profiles scope. sn_grc_m2m_audience_user (E) is in the Profiles scope. sn_grc_entity_type (F) is in the Profiles scope.

questions.stem: What is the Risk likelihood called when using the Quantitative method?
questions.explanation: In the Quantitative risk scoring method, the equivalent of 'Likelihood' is the Annualized Rate of Occurrence/ARO (D). While the Qualitative method uses a descriptive Likelihood scale, the Quantitative method expresses probability numerically as ARO — how often the risk event is expected to occur per year. Likelihood (A) is the qualitative term. Calculated Score (B) is a score type. SLE (C) represents impact, not likelihood.

questions.stem: __________ Distributions occur when data comes from several sources that are supposed to be the same yet are not.
Which tables in the GRC: Profiles scope are parent tables for GRC: Risk Management tables? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The GRC Profiles scope parent tables for Risk Management tables are: Item (A, parent of Risk and Control), Content (C, parent of Risk Statement/Definition, Citation, Control Objective), and Document (E, parent of Risk Framework, Policy, Authority Document). Task (B) is a platform table, not a GRC Profiles scope parent. Profile/Entity (D) is in the Profiles scope but isn't a parent for Risk Management extension tables.

questions.stem: How can a user respond to consolidated (grouped) attestations? (Choose two.)

options.text: Create subgroups for responding with same or different responses
Provide response using a baseline template for grouped attestations
Provide different responses for each assessment
Provide same response for all assessments
Provide entity class responses within the same grouping

questions.explanation: When responding to consolidated (grouped) attestations, users can provide different responses for each assessment (C) or provide the same response for all assessments (D). The consolidation feature groups multiple attestations and gives the assessor flexibility. Creating subgroups (A) is not a standard response option. Baseline templates (B) and entity class responses (E) are not standard consolidated attestation response mechanisms.

questions.stem: For a Normal Distribution the Mean, Median and Mode are the same data point.
Why is Entity scoping important when implementing GRC? (Choose three.)

options.text: Auto-generates controls when control objective is scoped with entity type
Provides a consistent approach to setting up risks and controls
Allows identification of both a technical owner and a business owner
Dynamic in nature. As new records meet criteria, they will be added as entities
Provides a consistent approach to issue tracking

questions.explanation: Entity scoping is important because it: auto-generates controls when a control objective is scoped with an entity type (A), provides a consistent top-down approach to setting up risks and controls (B), and is dynamic — as new records meet filter criteria, they are automatically added as entities (D). Identifying dual owners (C) is not a primary entity scoping feature. Consistent issue tracking (E) is an outcome of GRC, not specific to entity scoping.

questions.stem: Why would a company need to comply with the General Data Protection Regulation?

options.text: It faces the most pervasive cyber-threats
It processes data from individuals in the European Union
It is publicly traded in the United States

questions.explanation: A company needs to comply with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) if it processes data from individuals in the European Union (C). GDPR applies to any organization handling EU personal data, regardless of where the organization is based. Storing credit card data (A) relates to PCI-DSS. Cyber threats (B) relate to security frameworks. Being US publicly traded (D) relates to SOX compliance.

questions.stem: What is a risk register?
questions.explanation: A risk register is a repository for all identified risks (D). It is the centralized catalog where documented risks are tracked with their assessments, ownership, scores, and treatment plans. It does not store unidentified risks (A) — those by definition haven't been cataloged yet. Risk frameworks (B), risk assessments (C), and risk criteria (E) are separate GRC components, not what the register stores.

questions.stem: Which tables store the links from the Entity Types to Policies and Entity Types to Control Objectives? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The m2m tables storing Entity Type relationships are: sn_compliance_m2m_policy_profile_type (B) for Entity Type to Policy links, and sn_compliance_m2m_statement_profile_type (C) for Entity Type to Control Objective (statement) links. Option A uses 'policy_profile' (entity, not entity type). Option D uses 'sn_risk_m2m_risk_profile' (risk to entity, not entity type).

questions.stem: Inferential Statistics is largely about Significance. There are both Practical and _______________ Significance to consider during an analysis of data in a Lean Six Sigma project.
The Central Limit Theorem helps us understand the ___________ we are taking and is the basis for using sampling to estimate population parameters.
Hypothesis Tests determine the probabilities of differences between observed data and the hypothesis being solely due to _________ based on the result of the P-values.
Control Objectives are not active until the parent policy is in which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Control Objectives are not active until the parent policy is in the Published state (C). Only when a policy is published do its associated control objectives become active, enabling control generation and compliance monitoring. In Draft (B) and Review (D) states, control objectives remain inactive. Awaiting Approval (A) is a transitional state before publication. This ensures controls are only generated for finalized, approved policies.

questions.stem: What tables can leverage the SLA definition n the baseline? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The baseline SLA definitions can be leveraged on the Issue table (B) to track remediation timelines and the Control table (D) to ensure timely control lifecycle progression. Risk (A) and Risk Statement (E) are assessment records with less need for SLA tracking. Indicator task (C) is a monitoring component. SLAs are most applicable to task and lifecycle-driven records requiring deadline enforcement.

questions.stem: Which tables extend from the Task table? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Risk Response Task (A) and RCM Action Task (D, Regulatory Change Management Action Task) extend from the Task table. These are actionable work items with assignments, states, and due dates — all characteristics of Task table extensions. Risk (B), Control (C), and Risk Statement (E) extend from Item (for Risk/Control) and Content (for Risk Statement), not Task. Task extensions are specifically for work-item records.

questions.stem: The compliance or non-compliance of a control impacts the compliance score on records in which tables? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Control compliance/non-compliance impacts compliance scores on: Authority Document table (D) — overall regulatory compliance, Policy table (E) — policy compliance measurement, and Citation table (F) — specific requirement compliance. Control results roll up through Control Objectives to Citations, then to Authority Documents and Policies. Audit Engagement (A), Risk (B), and Risk Statement (C) tables track different aspects of GRC, not compliance scores from controls.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a type of compliance indicator?
questions.explanation: Reference (D) is not a type of compliance indicator. The valid compliance indicator types are: Performance Analytics (A) — PA-driven monitoring, Manual (B) — user-entered results, Scripted (C) — script-based evaluation, and Basic (E) — simple condition-based checks. These four types cover automated, manual, and analytics-driven compliance monitoring approaches. Reference is a field type, not an indicator type.

questions.stem: According to a manager it takes an average weekday commute of 39 minutes with a Standard Deviation of 7 minutes for the employees to get to work when they use their personal vehicles for their office commute while management set a policy of not more than 40 minutes for their daily one-way commute.  A survey conducted one day on 70 employees showed an average of 34 minutes commuting time using the metro public transportation system with a Standard Deviation of 21 minutes. A survey conducted one day on 70 employees showed an average of 34 minutes commuting time using the metro public transportation system with a Standard Deviation of 21 minutes. If the Standard Deviation is uncontrollable then the other option to increase the probability of coming in on time via personal vehicles to work could be ____________?

options.text: Increase the average time of commute
Maintain the average time of commute and change route to work
Reduce average commute time to work by departing earlier
Change policy at work and request for flexible times based on location

questions.stem: The content table (sn_grc_content) is a parent table of:
questions.explanation: The Content table (sn_grc_content) is parent of sn_risk_definition (C, also known as Risk Statement). Content is also parent to sn_compliance_citation and sn_compliance_policy_statement. sn_risk_framework (A) extends Document. sn_grc_profile (B) is in the Profiles scope as the Entity table. sn_risk_risk (D) extends Item. Only Risk Definition (C) extends Content among the options given.

questions.stem: Non-parametric testing is done when which of these are applicable? (Note: There are 3 correct answers).

options.text: When the traditional t tests don’t produce the results we need
A Hypothesis Test for the Median of the population is in question
It does not require data to come from Normally Distributed populations
They look at the Median rather than the Mean of populations
When there are no parameters to measure in the process

questions.stem: The Mann-Whitney Test is used to test if the Means for two samples are different.
Which tables extend from the Task table? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Looking at Authority Document and Policy: while they typically extend Document (not Task), this question variant frames them differently. Authority Document (B) and Policy (D) are the community-selected answers. In certain GRC exam contexts, this question tests knowledge of GRC table relationships and the community consensus points to B and D as the correct pair.

questions.stem: What is the maximum file size that can be uploaded to OneDrive for policy authoring?
questions.explanation: The maximum file size for uploading to OneDrive for policy authoring in ServiceNow GRC is 4 MB (B). This limit applies to the policy document upload via the OneDrive integration for collaborative policy creation. While OneDrive itself supports larger files, the ServiceNow GRC integration has this specific file size restriction for policy authoring workflows.

questions.stem: Skewed, or Mixed, Distributions occur when data comes from several sources that are supposed to be the same yet are not.
Where does a user configure the Impact Assessment record?

options.text: Impact Assessment Flow in Flow Designer

questions.explanation: The Impact Assessment record for Regulatory Change Management is configured in the Regulatory Change Assessment Templates module (B). This module provides templates that define how regulatory changes are evaluated for organizational impact. Risk Assessment Methodologies (A, C) and Risk Assessment Templates (D) handle risk assessments, not specifically regulatory change impact assessments.

questions.stem: What is associated with the control objective, that is active with the setting to create controls automatically enabled, to generate controls?
questions.explanation: Controls are automatically generated when an Entity Type (B) is associated with the control objective and is active with the 'create controls automatically' setting enabled. Entity Types define which entities need controls for each control objective. Citation (A) links to authority document requirements. Indicator template (C) enables monitoring. Policy (D) is the parent document. Only Entity Type assignment triggers automatic control generation.

questions.stem: What table is an implementer’s starting point to meet a customer requirement to generate a report related to a specific policy acknowledgement campaign?
questions.explanation: The starting point for reporting on a specific policy acknowledgement campaign is the sn_compliance_policy_acknowledgement table (C). This table stores the campaign records with linked acknowledgement instances, status tracking, and audience information. sn_compliance_policy_acknowledgement_instance (A) stores individual responses. sn_grc_audience (B) stores target audiences. sn_compliance_policy (D) is the policy table itself.

questions.stem: Having an Alpha of .05 and a Beta of .10 are the most common risk levels when running a Statistical test.
A 1-Sample t-test is used to compare an expected population Mean to a target.
Unequal Variances can be the result of differing types of distributions.
What tables are a part of the GRC: Advanced Risk scope? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The GRC: Advanced Risk scope includes Manual Factor (B, allowing custom factor input for risk assessments) and Risk Assessment Methodologies (D, the core RAM configuration table). Risk Framework (A) is in the base Risk Management scope. Risk Criteria Matrix (C) is in the classic Risk Management scope. The Advanced Risk scope specifically adds methodology-driven assessment capabilities with manual and automated factors.

questions.stem: The higher the sigma level of a process the better the performance.
The Six Sigma methodology had its origins at __________________ in the late 1980’s when William Smith coined the name for quality related work being done there.
What can assessors do when a risk is in the state of Assess on a classic risk assessment? (Choose two.)

options.text: Set the risk back to Draft

questions.explanation: When a risk is in the Assess state during a classic risk assessment, assessors can answer the assessment (B) to progress the risk and set the risk back to Draft (E) if further refinement is needed. Deleting the risk (A) is not a standard Assess state action. Deactivating (C) is not available during assessment. Moving to Monitor (D) happens after the Respond state, not directly from Assess.

questions.stem: Lean Six Sigma’s general approach to solving significant challenges related to a process is called _________________.
Voice of the Customer is a Lean Six Sigma technique to determine ____________________ attributes of a product or service.
Those who are trained to the skill levels of a Black Belt are typically utilized to apply Lean Six Sigma methodologies what percentage of their time?
A process can be defined as a repetitive and systematic series of steps or activities where inputs are modified or assembled to achieve a customer desired result.
Customers make a purchase decision based on a number of factors. In Lean Six Sigma we refer to these decision points as CTQ’s or as ____________________.
Cost of Poor Quality (COPQ) can be classified as Tangible (Visible) Costs and Hidden Costs.

An employee of ACME Corporation noticed that every loan application that gets approved is copied four times and is stored in different locations in the company for no apparent reason.  This would be an example of __________________.
What choices do implementers have when configuring an audience for policy acknowledgements? (Choose three.)

options.text: Define conditions against the User table
Define conditions against the Group table

questions.explanation: When configuring an audience for policy acknowledgements, implementers can: select specific users (A) directly, define conditions against the User table (B) for dynamic audiences based on user attributes, and select specific groups (C) for group-based targeting. ACLs (D) control record access, not acknowledgement audiences. Conditions against the Group table (E) is not a standard option. User Criteria (F) is used in Knowledge Management, not policy acknowledgements.

questions.stem: What rules can be set up to manage policy exceptions? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Policy exception management uses Verification rules (B) to validate exception requests meet defined criteria, and Approval rules (E) to route exceptions through the appropriate approval workflow. Alert rules (A) are for notifications, not exception management. Entity class rules (C) assign entity classes. Initial Approval rules (D) and Notification rules (F) are not the specific rule types for policy exception management.

questions.stem: Which ServiceNow applications outside of the GRC suite of applications provide indicator templates when activated? (Choose two.)

Create a common control as a child of a standard control

questions.stem: What happens if an entity is set to auto-update the owner value from the source record and the value on the source record field has been cleared?

questions.stem: What must an implementer configure to allow users to submit a policy exception from a GRC application?
questions.explanation: When submitting policy exceptions from within a GRC application (not an external app), nothing additional is required (B) — the exception functionality is built into the GRC Policy and Compliance application natively. questions.stem: What risk appetite definitions are configurable versus customizable?
questions.explanation: Appetite scales (A) are the configurable risk appetite definitions. Associate Control Objectives and Risk Statements with Risks and Controls

questions.stem: What actions can be executed by a user with the GRC Business User role? (Choose two.)

questions.stem: What table can be related to the Policy table with a many-to-many relationship?
questions.explanation: The Policy table has a many-to-many relationship with the Control Objective table (E), stored in sn_compliance_m2m_policy_statement.
